title: Ezekiel 3 — The scroll eaten, the ruach lifts the prophet, the watchman

verdicts.reasoning: ʾēṯ ʾăšer-timṣāʾ ʾĕḵôl ʾĕḵôl ʾeṯ-hamməḡillâ hazzōʾṯ: object-first 'what you find, eat; eat this scroll' preserves the Hebrew order. Exact.
wayyaʾăḵilēnî is Hiphil 'and he fed me'; correct.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (Raëlian canon; verified against the FR/EN quotation file)
verdicts.reasoning: biṭnəḵā ṯaʾăḵēl (Hiphil) 'feed your belly', ûmēʿêḵā ṯəmallēʾ 'fill your innards', kiḏḇaš ləmāṯôq 'like honey for sweetness': exact. Reception note accurately reports TBWTT ch. 3 on the sweetness and is labelled.
lek-bōʾ ... wəḏibbartā ḇiḏḇāray 'go, come ... speak with my words': the bə- of instrument is kept. Speech opens for 3:4-9.
ʿimqê śāp̄â wəḵiḇḏê lāšôn 'deep of lip and heavy of tongue' is literal where ASV paraphrases; sense explained (Isa 33:19). Correct.
ʾim-lōʾ read as asseverative 'Surely' is the standard analysis of the oath particle; 'whose words you cannot understand' renders lōʾ-ṯišmaʿ in its 'understand' sense.
ḥizqê-mēṣaḥ ûqəšê-lēḇ 'hard of forehead and stubborn of heart'; lōʾ yōʾḇû 'will not be willing'. Exact.

citations: Block, The Book of Ezekiel: Chapters 1-24 (NICOT, 1997), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: nāṯattî ʾeṯ-pānêḵā ḥăzāqîm ləʿummaṯ pənêhem 'I have made your face hard against their faces'; ḥzq wordplay on yəḥezqēʾl is widely noted. Correct.
kəšāmîr ḥāzāq miṣṣōr 'like adamant, harder than flint' (comparative min); ASV 'adamant' kept for the unidentified šāmîr. Speech closes correctly.
qaḥ bilḇāḇəḵā ûḇəʾāzəneḵā šəmāʿ 'take into your heart and hear with your ears', Hebrew order kept. Exact.
ʾel-haggôlâ 'to the exiles' (collective gôlâ) and the nested messenger formula are correct.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (Raëlian canon; verified against the FR/EN quotation file)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed wattiśśāʾēnî rûaḥ ... qôl raʿaš gāḏôl bārûḵ kəḇôḏ-YHWH mimməqômô. 'rumbling' is the lexical sense of raʿaš (quake/rumble, Nah 3:2 of wheels) where ASV 'rushing' is impressionistic; the MT bārûḵ is kept and the bərûm emendation (adopted by Zimmerli and NRSV, 'as the glory ... rose') is fully recorded, which is the declared baseline. The reception note correctly reports TBWTT ch. 3 (3:14 and 3:12 quoted as transport by the creators' craft) and the line stays lexical; 'his place' vs 'its place' is noted.
maššîqôṯ is Hiphil of nšq 'touching'; ʾiššâ ʾel-ʾăḥôṯāh reciprocal idiom; 'great rumbling' consistent with v 12 and with the wheel-noise collocation of Nah 3:2.

citations: Block, 'The Prophet of the Spirit: The Use of rwḥ in the Book of Ezekiel', JETS 32 (1989)
verdicts.reasoning: Two rûaḥ in one verse correctly split: wərûaḥ nəśāʾaṯnî (agent, 'ruach') vs baḥămaṯ rûḥî (the prophet's own temper, 'spirit'), exactly as the overlay rule states; mar 'bitter' and yaḏ-YHWH ... ḥāzāqâ are exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv wʾšr / Qere wāʾēšēḇ verified in the source: the only sense-changing pair, and the Qere 'and I sat where they were sitting' is translated (ASV follows the Ketiv). mašmîm 'stunned' (Hiphil participle šmm) and 'Tel-abib' (til abūbi) are correct.
The mid-verse pisqa is kept in the Hebrew and the English is not broken; davar-yhwh formula with colon. Correct.
ṣōp̄eh nəṯattîḵā 'I have made you a watchman'; wəhizhartā 'warn'. Exact; speech opens for 3:17-21.
môṯ tāmûṯ 'You shall surely die' (inf. abs. + finite) nested as quoted speech; dāmô miyyāḏəḵā ʾăḇaqqēš 'his blood I will require from your hand'. Exact.
ʾeṯ-nap̄šəḵā hiṣṣaltā 'you have delivered your life' diverges from ASV 'soul' on lexical grounds (nep̄eš as one's own life, saved from bloodguilt), matching NRSV/NJPS and the Kings practice.
ûḇəšûḇ ṣaddîq miṣṣiḏqô ... miḵšôl 'stumbling-block'; ṣiḏqōṯāw 'his righteous deeds' (plural); tizzāḵarnâ 'shall not be remembered'. Exact.
ḥāyô yiḥyeh kî nizhār 'he shall surely live, because he took warning'; 'delivered your life' as v 19. Speech closes correctly.
wattəhî ʿālay šām yaḏ-YHWH; qûm ṣēʾ ʾel-habbiqʿâ 'go out into the valley' (biqʿâ, central biq'ah-ha-atzamot). Exact.
kəḇôḏ-YHWH ʿōmēḏ ... kakkāḇôḏ ʾăšer rāʾîṯî ʿal-nəhar-kəḇār; central kavod-yhwh and nehar-kevar applied. Exact.

citations: Block, 'The Prophet of the Spirit: The Use of rwḥ in the Book of Ezekiel', JETS 32 (1989)
verdicts.reasoning: wattāḇōʾ-ḇî rûaḥ wattaʿămiḏēnî repeats 2:2 under the same rule; bōʾ hissāḡēr bəṯôḵ bêṯeḵā 'Go, shut yourself inside your house'. Correct.
nāṯənû ʿāleḵā ʿăḇôṯîm: the unidentified plural subject 'they' is kept without choosing between people and impersonal. Correct.
ûləšônəḵā ʾaḏbîq ʾel-ḥikkeḵā; wəneʾĕlamtā 'you shall be mute'; ʾîš môḵîaḥ 'a man who reproves'. Exact.
haššōmēaʿ yišmāʿ wəheḥāḏēl yeḥdāl 'He who hears, let him hear; and he who refrains, let him refrain'; speech of 3:24-27 closes correctly.

Founder decides (point C; verse flag at EZK-WOH-11:19).

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked every English line, with particular attention to the 16 reception-note sites (2:1, 2:10, 3:3, 3:12, 8:3, 11:1, 11:23, 40:2, 40:3, 42:14, 43:2, 44:2, 44:3, 44:15, 44:18, 44:30). No line carries the canon reading: kāḇôḏ stays 'glory' (11:23; 43:2), the bronze man keeps the Hebrew simile (40:3), qōḏeš stays 'holy' against the canon's 'healthful' (42:14), ʾûlām stays 'porch' against the 'airlock' reading (44:3), and yezaʿ is rendered by its accepted sense (44:18). Each reception note was checked against the TBWTT ch. 3 quotation file and is accurate and labelled, except that 11:23 slightly overstates the canon (verdict revise, notes only). Two features a cold reader might query were judged not to be leakage: 'ruach' (an inferred overlay convention that leaves an acknowledged ambiguity open and replaces the ASV's doctrinal capital) and 'between the land and the skies' at 8:3 (the ratified eretz default and shamayim physical register, identical to GEN-WOH 1:1, with the Hebrew's 'in visions of Elohim' kept). The sacrificial and architectural modernizations ('guilt-offering', 'dash', 'guardroom', 'vestibule', 'altar hearth') follow NRSV/NJPS and the lexica and carry no interpretive content.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 207 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 27 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, sources, overlay, central diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-e2-editor-report.md. After reading it no verdict changed. The report raises nothing on 11:19 (a new ruach), 11:23 (reception-note wording) or 44:24 (Ketiv wording in the line), so those stand. Spot-checks the report requested: NRSV 8:16 'temple', 42:1 'temple yard', 42:3 'in three stories', 43:15-16 'altar hearth', Yadin IEJ 8 (1958), the Mesha line-12 ʾrʾl, and Albright 1942 (ziggurat; arallû) are consistent with the reviewer's knowledge; the '43:3 six manuscripts' count and the exact LXX figure at 40:14 could not be confirmed independently and should be checked against BHS or worded as 'some manuscripts' / 'a different figure' (non-blocking). The report's Ketiv/Qere count (48 readings in 24 verses) matches the reviewer's independent count of 50 bracketed tokens.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-quotation-marks: Ratify the Kings convention for Ezekiel. The reviewer's own stack simulation confirms all eight chapters balance and the 43:7-17 boundary is defensible. Schedule a punctuation-only pass on ch. 37 (37:4-5, 9, 12-14, 16, 19, 21-28) and a check of chs. 1 and 10 so the book ships with one convention.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-proper-names: Keep English forms in Ezekiel for this wave: a mixed book would be worse than either practice, and the three signed-off chapters already use English. Recommendation for the corpus decision: the Latter Prophets volumes (isaiah-woh, ezekiel-woh, daniel-woh) already share English forms while genesis/exodus/Kings transliterate; record that genre split explicitly in a central convention note rather than converting Ezekiel, unless the founder wants decision A extended corpus-wide, in which case the mechanical pass over all eleven chapters is straightforward.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-ruach: Ratify the overlay rule for agent/transport rûaḥ, 'spirit' for human idioms and 'side' for the compass sense, and support merging it with the Kings ruach entries into one central entry. Before promotion, narrow the 'gift' clause: rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ paired with lēḇ (11:19; later 18:31; 36:26a) is the human disposition and should be 'a new spirit', while YHWH's own rûaḥ and the breath of life (36:27; 37:5-6, 14) stay 'ruach'. Verse flag at EZK-WOH-11:19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-inferred-temple-terms: Ship both as inferred. ʾêlām 'vestibule' (NRSV) and harʾēl/ʾăriʾêl 'altar hearth' (NRSV) are lexically supported, replace ASV renderings without lexical basis ('arches', 'upper altar'), and the disputes (40:30 plurals; the 'mountain of El' vocalization) are recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-sacrificial-vocabulary: Ratify the new central entry as direct. 'guilt-offering' and 'dash' are lexically motivated and match NRSV/NJPS and isaiah-woh; Milgrom's alternatives are correctly recorded but not adopted. Add the glossaryRef to EXO-WOH-20:21 and 1KI-WOH-8:63-64 at the next pass of those books.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-refId-prefix: Agree. Normalize EZK- to EZK-WOH- (and GEN- to GEN-WOH-) in one dedicated mechanical central op with a before/after count, separate from any content diff, and only after the Revelation and Ezekiel E2 diffs are both applied.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּמְצָ֖א אֱכ֑וֹל אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת־הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וְלֵ֥ךְ דַּבֵּ֖ר אֶל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, what you find, eat; eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."

notes.official: *ʾēṯ ʾăšer-timṣāʾ ʾĕḵôl* 'what you find, eat' (ASV 'eat that which thou findest'): the object comes first for emphasis, and the next clause names it as 'this scroll' (`megillat-sefer-scroll-written-front-and-back-ezekiel-2-3`).

paragraphs.text: וָאֶפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־פִּ֑י וַיַּ֣אֲכִלֵ֔נִי אֵ֖ת הַמְּגִלָּ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

i18n.en: So I opened my mouth, and he fed me this scroll.

notes.official: *wayyaʾăḵilēnî* 'and he fed me' is the Hiphil 'caused me to eat' (ASV). The prophet opens his mouth, and the feeding is done to him.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ בִּטְנְךָ֤ תַֽאֲכֵל֙ וּמֵעֶ֣יךָ תְמַלֵּ֔א אֵ֚ת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֣ן אֵלֶ֑יךָ וָאֹ֣כְלָ֔ה וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק׃ (פ)

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, feed your belly and fill your innards with this scroll that I am giving you." So I ate it, and it was in my mouth like honey for sweetness.

notes.official:
*biṭnəḵā ṯaʾăḵēl ûmēʿêḵā ṯəmallēʾ* 'feed your belly and fill your innards': *mēʿîm* are the inward parts, the seat of feeling (Isa 16:11; Jer 4:19). *kiḏḇaš ləmāṯôq* 'like honey for sweetness'. The image of the word as sweet food recurs at Jer 15:16 and Ps 19:11 [ET 19:10]; Rev 10:9-10 takes it up and adds bitterness in the belly.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness') and reads the sweetness as the prophet's response to what he learns from the scroll. The line renders the Hebrew lexically.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם לֶךְ־בֹּא֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ בִדְבָרַ֖י אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, go, come to the house of Israel, and speak with my words to them.

notes.official: *wəḏibbartā ḇiḏḇāray ʾălêhem* 'and speak with my words to them': the prophet speaks with YHWH's own words, the words he has just eaten. The speech runs to 3:9.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֡י לֹא֩ אֶל־עַ֨ם עִמְקֵ֥י שָׂפָ֛ה וְכִבְדֵ֥י לָשׁ֖וֹן אַתָּ֣ה שָׁל֑וּחַ אֶל־בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: For you are not sent to a people deep of lip and heavy of tongue — to the house of Israel;

notes.official: *ʿimqê śāp̄â wəḵiḇḏê lāšôn* 'deep of lip and heavy of tongue' is rendered literally. It means a people whose speech cannot be understood (cf. Isa 33:19 *ʿimqê śāp̄â*). The ASV paraphrases: 'of a strange speech and of a hard language'.

paragraphs.text: לֹ֣א ׀ אֶל־עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ וְכִבְדֵ֣י לָשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־תִשְׁמַ֖ע דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם אִם־לֹ֤א אֲלֵיהֶם֙ שְׁלַחְתִּ֔יךָ הֵ֖מָּה יִשְׁמְע֥וּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: not to many peoples deep of lip and heavy of tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I had sent you to them, they would listen to you.

notes.official: *ʾim-lōʾ ʾălêhem šəlaḥtîḵā hēmmâ yišməʿû ʾēleḵā*: *ʾim-lōʾ* works here as an asseverative ('surely'), as in oath formulas (GKC §149). The line has 'Surely, if I had sent you to them, they would listen to you'; the ASV has 'surely, if I sent thee to them, they would hearken unto thee'.

paragraphs.text: וּבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א יֹאבוּ֙ לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־אֵינָ֥ם אֹבִ֖ים לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלָ֑י כִּ֚י כָּל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי־מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי־לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה׃

i18n.en: But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me; for all the house of Israel are hard of forehead and stubborn of heart.

notes.official: *ḥizqê-mēṣaḥ ûqəšê-lēḇ* 'hard of forehead and stubborn of heart' is literal (cf. 2:4). The house of Israel's refusal to listen to the prophet is a refusal to listen to YHWH ('for they are not willing to listen to me').

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֧תִּי אֶת־פָּנֶ֛יךָ חֲזָקִ֖ים לְעֻמַּ֣ת פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶֽת־מִצְחֲךָ֥ חָזָ֖ק לְעֻמַּ֥ת מִצְחָֽם׃

i18n.en: Behold, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their foreheads.

notes.official: *nāṯattî ʾeṯ-pānêḵā ḥăzāqîm ləʿummaṯ pənêhem* 'I have made your face hard against their faces'. *ḥāzāq* 'hard, strong' repeats the root of the prophet's name (*yəḥezqēʾl*, 'El strengthens'); the wordplay is widely noted (Zimmerli; Block, *Ezekiel 1-24*, NICOT).

paragraphs.text: כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ לֹֽא־תִירָ֤א אוֹתָם֙ וְלֹא־תֵחַ֣ת מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֛י בֵּֽית־מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Like adamant, harder than flint, I have made your forehead. Do not fear them, and do not be dismayed at their faces, for they are a rebellious house."

notes.official: *kəšāmîr ḥāzāq miṣṣōr* 'like adamant, harder than flint'. *šāmîr* is a stone harder than flint, used for engraving (Jer 17:1 'with a point of *šāmîr*'; Zech 7:12); it is identified with emery or diamond. The ASV 'adamant' is kept because it names 'the hardest stone' without choosing between the two. The speech of 3:4-9 closes here.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרַי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ קַ֥ח בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְאָזְנֶ֥יךָ שְׁמָֽע׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, all my words that I will speak to you, take into your heart and hear with your ears.

notes.official: A new speech (3:10-11). *qaḥ bilḇāḇəḵā ûḇəʾāzəneḵā šəmāʿ* 'take into your heart and hear with your ears': the order (heart before ears) is the Hebrew's.

paragraphs.text: וְלֵ֨ךְ בֹּ֤א אֶל־הַגּוֹלָה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה אִֽם־יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם־יֶחְדָּֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: Go, come to the exiles, to the sons of your people, and speak to them and say to them, 'Thus says the Lord YHWH,' whether they hear or whether they refrain."

notes.official: *ʾel-haggôlâ* 'to the exiles' (ASV 'to them of the captivity'): *gôlâ* is the collective 'exile, community of exiles'. *bənê ʿammeḵā* 'the sons of your people'. The messenger formula is set in single quotes inside the divine speech (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ וָאֶשְׁמַ֣ע אַחֲרַ֔י ק֖וֹל רַ֣עַשׁ גָּד֑וֹל בָּר֥וּךְ כְּבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Then ruach lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of YHWH from his place!" —

notes.official:
*wattiśśāʾēnî rûaḥ* 'then ruach lifted me up': as at 2:2, *rûaḥ* has no article and is the agent (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`; ASV 'the Spirit').

*qôl raʿaš gāḏôl* 'the sound of a great rumbling'. *raʿaš* is quaking or rumbling: the earthquake (1 Kgs 19:11-12; Amos 1:1), the rattle of chariot wheels (Nah 3:2 *qôl raʿaš ʾôp̄ān*; Jer 47:3), the rattling of a javelin (Job 41:21 [ET 41:29]). In v 13 the noise comes from the wings and the wheels, the Nahum collocation. The KJV/ASV 'a great rushing' renders the impression of motion rather than the root; NRSV has 'the sound of loud rumbling' (`raash-gadol-great-rumbling-ezekiel-3`). At 37:7 the same noun is 'a rattling', of bones coming together.

*bārûḵ kəḇôḏ-YHWH mimməqômô* 'Blessed be the glory of YHWH from his place!' is the MT. A widely adopted emendation (S. D. Luzzatto; Cornill; NRSV) reads *bərûm* for *bārûḵ* (one letter, kaph for mem): 'as the glory of YHWH rose from its place', which matches the departure scenes of 10:4, 18-19. The MT can be construed as a doxology heard in the noise, and it is translated without the ASV's supplied '[saying]' (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). The suffix of *məqômô* may refer to YHWH ('his place') or to the glory ('its place'). The line keeps the ASV's 'his', which goes with the doxology; the emended text would require 'its'. The verse is the source of the *Qedushah* response in the synagogue liturgy.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes 3:14 and 3:12 ('The spirit lifted me up; it took me away ... I heard behind me a voice of a great rushing') and reads them as the prophet being carried by the creators' craft. The line follows the book's rûaḥ convention and renders *raʿaš* by its lexical sense; the craft reading belongs to this note.

paragraphs.text: וְק֣וֹל ׀ כַּנְפֵ֣י הַחַיּ֗וֹת מַשִּׁיקוֹת֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אֶל־אֲחוֹתָ֔הּ וְק֥וֹל הָאוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וְק֖וֹל רַ֥עַשׁ גָּדֽוֹל׃

i18n.en: and the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, and the sound of a great rumbling.

notes.official: *wəqôl kanp̄ê haḥayyôṯ maššîqôṯ ʾiššâ ʾel-ʾăḥôṯāh* 'and the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching one another'. *maššîqôṯ* is a Hiphil of *nāšaq* 'kiss', so 'touching'. *ʾiššâ ʾel-ʾăḥôṯāh* ('a woman to her sister') is the reciprocal idiom of 1:9, 23 (`chayyot`). *wəqôl hāʾôp̄annîm ləʿummāṯām* 'the sound of the wheels beside them'. *qôl raʿaš gāḏôl* closes the verse as in v 12: 'a great rumbling' (`raash-gadol-great-rumbling-ezekiel-3`), the noise of wheels as in Nah 3:2.

paragraphs.text: וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי וָאֵלֵ֥ךְ מַר֙ בַּחֲמַ֣ת רוּחִ֔י וְיַד־יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה׃

i18n.en: Ruach lifted me up and took me, and I went bitter, in the heat of my spirit; and the hand of YHWH was strong upon me.

notes.official: *wərûaḥ nəśāʾaṯnî wattiqqāḥēnî* 'ruach lifted me up and took me' (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`). The second *rûaḥ* of the verse, *baḥămaṯ rûḥî* 'in the heat of my spirit', is the prophet's own temper, and the overlay entry renders that idiom 'spirit'. *wāʾēlēḵ mar* 'and I went bitter'. *wəyaḏ-YHWH ʿālay ḥāzāqâ* 'and the hand of YHWH was strong upon me' (`yad-yhwh`) uses *ḥzq* again (cf. 3:8-9). For the canon's quotation of this verse see the reception note at 3:12.

paragraphs.text: וָאָב֨וֹא אֶל־הַגּוֹלָ֜ה תֵּ֣ל אָ֠בִיב הַיֹּשְׁבִ֤ים אֶֽל־נְהַר־כְּבָר֙ ואשר [וָֽאֵשֵׁ֔ב] הֵ֖מָּה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים שָׁ֑ם וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

i18n.en: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who were dwelling by the river Kebar, and I sat where they were sitting; and I sat there seven days, stunned, among them.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *wʾšr* ('and which, where') / Qere *wāʾēšēḇ* 'and I sat'. The Qere is translated ('and I sat where they were sitting') under `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`. This is the only Qere in the wave that changes the sense. The ASV follows the Ketiv ('and to where they dwelt').

*tēl ʾāḇîḇ* 'Tel-abib', in the ASV form (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-ezekiel`), is usually explained from Akkadian *til abūbi* 'mound of the flood', a common name type for ancient ruin-mounds in Babylonia (Zimmerli; Block). The modern city took its name from this verse (Sokolow's 1902 Hebrew title for Herzl's *Altneuland*). The exiles live 'by the river Kebar' (`nehar-kevar`).

*mašmîm* 'stunned' is a Hiphil participle of *šmm* 'be appalled, desolate' (ASV 'overwhelmed'). Seven days is the length of mourning (Gen 50:10; Job 2:13).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (פ) וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: At the end of seven days, the word of YHWH came to me, saying:

notes.official: The source has a *pisqa bəʾemṣaʿ pāsûq*, a Masoretic paragraph break in the middle of the verse: *(p)* stands after 'At the end of seven days' and before 'the word of YHWH came to me'. The mark is kept in the Hebrew text, and the English is not broken (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). The break sets off the watchman oracle (3:16b-21), which is repeated almost word for word at 33:7-9. *wayhî ḏəḇar-YHWH ʾēlay lēʾmōr* 'the word of YHWH came to me, saying' (`davar-yhwh-prophetic-formula`).

paragraphs.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֤ מִפִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר וְהִזְהַרְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

i18n.en: "Son of human, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; you shall hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me.

notes.official: *ṣōp̄eh nəṯattîḵā ləḇêṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel': the *ṣōp̄eh* is the lookout on a city wall (2 Sam 18:24-27; 2 Kgs 9:17-20). *wəhizhartā* 'and warn' (*zhr* Hiphil) is the key verb of 3:17-21. The speech runs to 3:21.

paragraphs.text: בְּאָמְרִ֤י לָֽרָשָׁע֙ מ֣וֹת תָּמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א הִזְהַרְתּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֥א דִבַּ֛רְתָּ לְהַזְהִ֥יר רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֥וֹ הָרְשָׁעָ֖ה לְחַיֹּת֑וֹ ה֤וּא רָשָׁע֙ בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: When I say to the wicked, 'You shall surely die,' and you do not warn him, and do not speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to keep him alive, he, the wicked, shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require from your hand.

notes.official: *môṯ tāmûṯ* 'you shall surely die' (infinitive absolute plus finite verb, as Gen 2:17) is the formula of a death sentence, quoted here inside the divine speech. *dāmô miyyāḏəḵā ʾăḇaqqēš* 'his blood I will require from your hand' is the formula of bloodguilt (Gen 9:5; 42:22).

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּה֙ כִּֽי־הִזְהַ֣רְתָּ רָשָׁ֔ע וְלֹא־שָׁב֙ מֵֽרִשְׁע֔וֹ וּמִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ הָרְשָׁעָ֑ה ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But you — if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness and from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your life.

notes.official: *wəʾattâ ʾeṯ-nap̄šəḵā hiṣṣāltā* 'but you have delivered your life'. Here *nep̄eš* is the person's own life, which the watchman saves from the bloodguilt of v 18. The ASV 'delivered thy soul' brings in the later sense of an immortal soul. The overlay entry `nefesh-scope-ezekiel` renders it 'life', following the Kings practice (NJPS and NRSV also 'life').

paragraphs.text: וּבְשׁ֨וּב צַדִּ֤יק מִצִּדְקוֹ֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֔וֶל וְנָתַתִּ֥י מִכְשׁ֛וֹל לְפָנָ֖יו ה֣וּא יָמ֑וּת כִּ֣י לֹ֤א הִזְהַרְתּוֹ֙ בְּחַטָּאת֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א תִזָּכַ֗רְןָ צִדְקֹתָו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: And when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does injustice, and I put a stumbling-block before him, he shall die; because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sin, and his righteous deeds that he did shall not be remembered; but his blood I will require from your hand.

notes.official: *ûḇəšûḇ ṣaddîq miṣṣiḏqô* 'and when a righteous man turns from his righteousness'. *wənāṯattî miḵšôl ləp̄ānāyw* 'and I put a stumbling-block before him'. *miḵšôl* is one of Ezekiel's characteristic terms (7:19; 14:3-4, 7; 18:30; 44:12). *ṣiḏqōṯāw* 'his righteous deeds' is the plural.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה כִּ֧י הִזְהַרְתּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֗יק לְבִלְתִּ֥י חֲטֹ֛א צַדִּ֖יק וְה֣וּא לֹא־חָטָ֑א חָי֤וֹ יִֽחְיֶה֙ כִּ֣י נִזְהָ֔ר וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But you — if you warn the righteous man that the righteous should not sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live, because he took warning; and you have delivered your life."

notes.official: *ḥāyô yiḥyeh kî nizhār* 'he shall surely live, because he took warning' mirrors 'you shall surely die' of v 18. *wəʾattâ ʾeṯ-nap̄šəḵā hiṣṣāltā* 'and you have delivered your life', as in v 19 (`nefesh-scope-ezekiel`). The watchman speech closes here.

paragraphs.text: וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד־יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י ק֥וּם צֵא֙ אֶל־הַבִּקְעָ֔ה וְשָׁ֖ם אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אוֹתָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: The hand of YHWH was upon me there, and he said to me, "Arise, go out into the valley, and there I will speak with you."

notes.official: *wattəhî ʿālay šām yaḏ-YHWH* 'the hand of YHWH was upon me there' (`yad-yhwh`). *ṣēʾ ʾel-habbiqʿâ* 'go out into the valley': *biqʿâ* is the open plain, the same noun as 37:1-2 (`biq'ah-ha-atzamot`). Commentators (Greenberg, AB 22) connect the two valley scenes.

paragraphs.text: וָאָקוּם֮ וָאֵצֵ֣א אֶל־הַבִּקְעָה֒ וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֤ם כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֔ד כַּכָּב֕וֹד אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי עַל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר וָאֶפֹּ֖ל עַל־פָּנָֽי׃

i18n.en: So I arose and went out into the valley, and behold — the glory of YHWH was standing there, like the glory that I had seen by the river Kebar; and I fell on my face.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh-šām kəḇôḏ-YHWH ʿōmēḏ* 'the glory of YHWH was standing there' (`kavod-yhwh`), 'like the glory that I had seen by the river Kebar' (`nehar-kevar`): this ties the scene back to the throne-vision of ch. 1. The prophet falls on his face as at 1:28.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹא־בִ֣י ר֔וּחַ וַתַּעֲמִדֵ֖נִי עַל־רַגְלָ֑י וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר אֹתִי֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֹּ֥א הִסָּגֵ֖ר בְּת֥וֹךְ בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And ruach came into me and set me on my feet, and he spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.

notes.official: *wattāḇōʾ-ḇî rûaḥ wattaʿămiḏēnî ʿal-raḡlāy* 'and ruach came into me and set me on my feet' repeats 2:2 (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`). *hissāḡēr bəṯôḵ bêṯeḵā* 'shut yourself inside your house'. The speech runs to 3:27.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם הִנֵּ֨ה נָתְנ֤וּ עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ עֲבוֹתִ֔ים וַאֲסָר֖וּךָ בָּהֶ֑ם וְלֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

i18n.en: And you, son of human — behold, they will put cords upon you and bind you with them, and you shall not go out among them.

notes.official: *hinnēh nāṯənû ʿāleḵā ʿăḇôṯîm* 'behold, they will put cords upon you'. The subject 'they' is not identified: it may be the people, or the plural may be impersonal ('cords will be put on you'). The line keeps the Hebrew's plural without choosing.

paragraphs.text: וּלְשֽׁוֹנְךָ֙ אַדְבִּ֣יק אֶל־חִכֶּ֔ךָ וְנֶֽאֱלַ֔מְתָּ וְלֹא־תִֽהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ מוֹכִ֑יחַ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃

i18n.en: I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, and you shall be mute, and you shall not be to them a man who reproves; for they are a rebellious house.

notes.official: *ûləšônəḵā ʾaḏbîq ʾel-ḥikkeḵā* 'I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth' (*ḥēḵ* 'palate'). *wəneʾĕlamtā* 'and you shall be mute'. *ləʾîš môḵîaḥ* 'a man who reproves', or an arbiter (cf. Job 9:33). The muteness is lifted at 24:27 and 33:22.

paragraphs.text: וּֽבְדַבְּרִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶפְתַּ֣ח אֶת־פִּ֔יךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ ׀ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל ׀ יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, 'Thus says the Lord YHWH.' He who hears, let him hear; and he who refrains, let him refrain; for they are a rebellious house."

notes.official: *haššōmēaʿ yišmāʿ wəheḥāḏēl yeḥdāl* 'He who hears, let him hear; and he who refrains, let him refrain' takes up the pair of 2:5, 7 and 3:11. The messenger formula is in single quotes. The speech of 3:24-27 closes here.
